comments.note: IDbConnection.ConnectionString in System.Data has an [AllowNull] annotation on its setter. FakeDbConnection's property needed [AllowNull] to satisfy the TreatWarningsAsErrors=true build. Future fakes implementing IDbConnection must apply the same pattern.

InMemorySpdbConfigRepository adds Has() and GetRaw() helpers beyond the interface contract for convenient test assertions. These should not proliferate if the repository grows; consider a ITestableSpdbConfigRepository marker or testability extensions pattern instead.

summary: Build: Release build clean — all 4 projects compile under TreatWarningsAsErrors=true with zero warnings.

AC-1: 48/48 tests pass (27 VideoIndexer.Tests + 21 VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.Tests), zero skipped. Count exceeds the 41 M1 baseline because M2 WPs added tests; the M1 baseline is fully intact with no regressions.
AC-2: All 5 fixture types are internal sealed and fully nullable-annotated. FakeDbConnection.ConnectionString carries [AllowNull] to satisfy IDbConnection contract under TreatWarningsAsErrors=true.

AC-3: InMemorySpdbConfigRepository implements ISpdbConfigRepository.GetAsync and SetAsync. Has() provides exists semantics; SchemaPresent=false triggers InvalidOperationException on all ops to simulate ConfigTableMissing.
AC-4: FakeDbConnectionFactory.Success() returns a controllable no-op IDbConnection; FakeDbConnectionFactory.Throws(exception) routes to Task.FromException — both code paths verified.

Edge-case stress: TempDirectory.Dispose guards Directory.Exists before deletion (safe on test failure); Throws() uses Task.FromException (avoids sync throw, correct async exception propagation); InMemorySpdbConfigRepository uses StringComparer.Ordinal (correct for config key semantics).

comments.note: InMemorySpdbConfigRepository uses a plain Dictionary<string,string> with no thread-safety guarantees. Acceptable for unit tests (single-threaded), but worth noting if parallel test execution is ever enabled.

The M1 AC baseline is stated as 41/41, but the actual passing count is now 48/48 due to tests added across M2 work packages (WP-003/WP-004). Consider updating the AC wording in future WPs to say 'no fewer than N tests pass' rather than an exact count to avoid confusion as the suite grows.
No observations beyond the above — fixtures are clean, well-structured, and consistent with project conventions.
